content: 1. Interim Sodium Reduction Targets for Flatbreads: An interim sodium target of 445 mg/100g has been established for all types of leavened and unleavened flatbreads, including tortillas, wraps, pita, Greek flatbreads, and naan. This target is to be achieved within four years, followed by further reductions toward global benchmarks. Refrigerated and frozen doughs are included, but pancakes are excluded. 2. Fish and Seafood Products: This category includes fish and seafood such as sardines, mackerel, shrimp, crab, clams, and smoked oysters, as well as retort-packed products. Canned anchovies are excluded. An interim sodium target of 450 mg/100g is set for processed fish and seafood products, including seasoned, breaded, battered, or stuffed fish, as well as imitation seafood like surimi. This target is to be achieved within four years, with further reductions planned. 3. Processed Meat Products: For raw and prepared meat products, including burgers, fresh sausages, and marinated or breaded meats, an interim sodium target of 485 mg/100g has been set. This target is to be achieved within four years, with subsequent reductions based on compliance reviews. Less than one-third of products currently meet the WHO benchmark. 4. Sauces, Dips, and Dressings: Sodium benchmarks have been established for various subcategories, including bouillon, soup stocks, pasta sauces, and salad dressings. For example, bouillon cubes and soup stock powders have a target of 1500 mg/100g, while mayonnaise-based dressings have a target of 500 mg/100g. Interim targets aim to reduce sodium content over three to four years, with further reductions planned. 5. Snack Foods: Sodium benchmarks for snacks such as crackers, nuts, chips, and extruded snacks have been set. For example, salted nuts and seeds have an interim target of 430 mg/100g, while chips and crisps have a target of 500 mg/100g. These targets are designed to drive reformulation efforts and align with global benchmarks. 6. Instant Noodles: A separate category has been established for instant noodles with sauce or seasoning (dry mix or concentrated). The sodium benchmark is reported as sold rather than as prepared. An interim target of 1730 mg/100g is recommended to be achieved within four years, with further reductions planned toward the global target of 770 mg/100g. 7. Bread and Bakery Products: Sodium benchmarks for bread and bakery products include 310 mg/100g for ordinary bread and 445 mg/100g for leavened bread. These targets are to be achieved within four years, with further reductions based on compliance reviews. 8. Seafood and Meat-Based Snacks: A new category has been established for seafood and meat-based snacks, such as fish or squid snacks and pork-based snacks. An interim sodium target of 1540 mg/100g is recommended to be achieved within four years, with further reductions planned. 9. Data Limitations: For certain food categories, such as smoked fish, dried fish, and some meat products, recommendations could not be made due to limited data availability. Interim targets may be considered based on available data. 10. Global Sodium Reduction Efforts: The document references global sodium benchmarks and highlights the importance of reducing sodium intake to align with public health goals. It emphasizes the need for reformulation of processed foods and the establishment of realistic interim targets to drive progress.
